rows.reaction: A caretaker delivering supplies sounds concrete. The four-week choices and character history mean little to me, so I will leave them empty.
I can see the building and a specific delivery. I will go to the bakery first.
The order count dropped and he thanked me; that feels like a delivery. I like that time pauses for the conversation.
Deliveries are easy to follow and the residents have distinct voices. I am curious what comes after the orders.
All five orders are done, even though Derya was out. Hanging the bread on her door is a clear result. I will see what skip does.
I am at flat 3 but the parcel is still an order and it says go to flat 3 again. I am unsure whether I should tap it again.
Feedback let me select I am confused; Escape returned to the menu. I saw no Back button and sent nothing.
Now it says I am waiting with a parcel. That explains why it remains, though the go button still looks odd.
I tapped the table job but the parcel stayed selected. I do not know why I cannot switch to the other job.
Tapping her flat let me do the table job. I am surprised it says the work is done while she is out, since she asked for help carrying it.
The deliveries were pleasant, but I am starting to feel I am just waiting for the next small job. I would stop for now.
I am stopping for now; the small jobs have begun to feel repetitive.
The same introduction is much wider here, though the fixed start button covers the lower text. I will try a different approach to the people this time.
I recognize the names and the same building: Tarık is in flat 7, as on the phone, and Sevim is in flat 2. I am confident because the labels match. The first order is Sevim rather than Tarık.
Sevim says the same on-time line I remember from the phone, with the same name and flat; I am confident it is the same resident. Opening the gate got a witnessed action but no judgment yet.
I like seeing the gate recorded as something I did. The notebook says a lemon candy detail after Sevim called Tarık kind; I am guessing that is the new line.
Hacer says exactly the same thing about Tarık as Sevim. That takes some life out of the conversation for me.
The larger building is easier to read. I am more interested in the residents than repeating the delivery route, but the repeated remark made them feel less distinct.
I have seen enough for tonight. The same delivery start and another conversation ending much like Tarık’s make me want to stop.

I am stopping tonight; I have had enough of the repeated start and similar conversations.
